messages:
alex: Heads-up — Acme procurement sent back the POC orderform with a couple of blockers: they want to attach their PO PDF to the DocuSign envelope and they added an HSM/KMS clause into the DPA. They also asked whether a PO can serve as an 'order acceptance' or if we still need DocuSign countersignature from our side.

maria (Sales Ops): They need the PO attached because their AP team refuses to process invoices without the signed PO on file. Can we do signer attachments in our envelope?

docu-sign-bot: FYI DocuSign: classic signer attachments are supported but not all template APIs preserve attachments when using certain composite templates. If using REST envelopes, include signerAttachment tabs or upload as supportingDocument in the envelope creation call. Could be brittle with our Node SDK v2.2.

tim (SE): Technical note re: KMS: we can document key management options in the DPA: we support customer-managed keys via KMS/HSM for Private deployments only. Hosted customers can bring keys to the KMS integration but we do not support per-tenant HSM-backed keys on hosted tier today.

jen (Legal): On the PO-as-acceptance question: we can accept a PO as an order if the PO explicitly references the MSA and contains identical material terms + our acceptance language. Preferable flow: 1) include an explicit acceptance clause in the orderform; 2) countersign via DocuSign for legal audit trail. That satisfies most procurement/legal teams.

ben (Finance): Also need the invoice routing code and tax ID on the attached PO for AP. Ask Acme for: "Bill to company name, remit address, tax ID, PO number, payment terms (Net30/Net45)" before we create invoice.

alex: I pushed back asking if they'd accept electronic attachment in the envelope (PDF) instead of trying to submit separately. They said AP will only accept if the attachment is inside the signed envelope.

maria (Sales Ops): Proposed envelope flow: - Create a DocuSign envelope using our template (Orderform v3) - Add supportingDocument: customer_PO.pdf as a document (not signer attachment) - Use signer tabs for Customer Signer -> Our Sales Rep -> Legal Exec (only if value >50k). That should keep the PO embedded.

tim (SE): Quick config snippet for engineering to generate envelope (example):
```
const envelope = {
  documents: [ { documentBase64: customerPoBase64, name: 'Acme_PO.pdf', documentId: '1' }, { documentBase64: orderformBase64, name: 'Orderform.pdf', documentId: '2' } ],
  recipients: { signers: [ /* customer signer */ ] },
  // set supportingDocument flags as required by API
};
```

jen (Legal): Two legal asks: 1) Add explicit acceptance sentence in the Orderform: "Redwood's countersignature or explicit electronic acceptance constitutes acceptance of this Purchase Order and incorporation of the Orderform terms." 2) For the DPA/KMS language: add an appendix that clarifies Hosted vs Private behavior and a checkbox for "Customer-managed KMS" if Private. I can draft.

ben (Finance): If they insist PO attached in envelope, confirm whether PO needs to be the first document in the envelope (their AP sometimes flags otherwise). Maria — can we make document order 1=PO, 2=Orderform?

maria (Sales Ops): Yes — we'll put PO as doc 1. Also ask Acme if they need an invoice immediately upon signing or after deployment milestone. That affects billing timing.

alex: Next steps: Jen to post a 1-page redline of the Orderform + DPA appendix. Tim to share the envelope sample with eng to ensure SDK flags preserve supportingDocument. Maria will ask Acme for billing fields and confirm if exec sign is required above $50k. Ben will confirm invoicing account number. I'll coordinate and circulate final envelope before sending.

jen (Legal): I'll have the redline by EOD PST and include the acceptance sentence + KMS appendix language.

tim (SE): I'll validate the Node and Python SDK flows tomorrow AM and add a small test harness to ensure attachments show up in the completed envelope PDF.

docu-sign-bot: Reminder: if you attach the PO as a separate document, include documentId ordering and set 'documentVisibility' appropriately so only intended recipients see it.

alex: Great — thanks everyone. If anyone wants to pair on the envelope test ping me. :thumbsup:
